NO CABIN YET
Week 7 · Clear and Natural Pronunciation

Captain Speaking

"Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking." Pilots don't have perfect accents, but everyone understands them. That's because they use clear stress, short pauses and clear word endings. On the DET, pronunciation is scored in every speaking question. This week you'll practise the three things that make the biggest difference for Japanese speakers. Every activity has a Fly again button. There's no grade, and finishing the steps counts as attending this week.

STOP 01~1 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the words, the announcements and how long you speak. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

Sound check:
STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET SCORING · PRONUNCIATION

The DET has four speaking questions: Speak About the Photo, Read, Then Speak, Interactive Speaking and the Speaking Sample. All four are scored on pronunciation and fluency. The goal is not a perfect accent. The goal is to be easy to understand. Match each skill to its description: tap a name, then tap its description.

STOP 03~5 min

Stress Test

DET SKILL · WORD STRESS

In katakana, every sound has the same length: ホ・テ・ル. In English, every word has one strong beat: ho-TEL. The strong beat is louder, longer and higher. A wrong stress can make a word hard to understand, even when every sound is correct. Tap the strong part of each word, then listen.

TIPSay the word quietly two ways before you tap: HO-tel… ho-TEL… Which one sounds like English?
STOP 04~4 min

Excess Baggage

DET SKILL · CLEAR ENDINGS

Katakana adds a vowel after most consonants: desk → デ・ス・ク. Those extra vowels are excess baggage. They add beats, and the listener may hear a different word. How many beats does the English word have? Count the vowel sounds, not the letters.

TIPPut your hand under your chin and say the word. Each time your chin drops is one beat. "Strike" drops once, but ス・ト・ラ・イ・ク drops five times!
STOP 05~8 min

Captain's Announcement

DET SKILL · SENTENCE STRESS & RHYTHM

In a sentence, the important words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, numbers) are strong. Small words like the, a, to, of, is, and are quick and weak. English also comes in short groups with a tiny pause between them. First tap the strongest words. Then listen, and shadow: read along with the voice at the same time.

STOP 06~8 min

Full Flight

DET PRACTICE · READ, THEN SPEAK

In Read, Then Speak, you read a topic with 2–3 questions, get 20 seconds to prepare, then speak for up to 90 seconds. Choose one pronunciation focus before you start, and record on Vocaroo (free, no account needed). Paste your link so I can listen.

STOP 07~2 min

Landing Card
